title: Eval scenario (v1alpha2: typed communication invocation)
description: One deterministic scenario inside an eval suite. v1alpha2 adds typed communication invocation (invoke: event | events | externalWebhook - the runner owns envelope construction, signing, publication and receipts through the SAME engine hg event uses) and runner-checked destination expectations (expect.outputs). `prompt` and `invoke` are mutually exclusive; `evaluate` becomes optional when `expect` carries the whole assertion. The evaluator exit-code protocol is unchanged: 0 pass, 1 assertion failure, anything else evaluator/harness error.

name.description: Unique within the suite (the runner enforces uniqueness across scenarios; the schema cannot see siblings).

profile.description: The deployed profile this scenario addresses — resolved against the onboarded catalogue, never an implicit global agent.

description.description: Free-text explanation of what the scenario proves, for readers; the runner does not interpret it.

prompt.description: Path (relative to the scenario directory, contained within it) to a prompt file the runner sends to the profile before the evaluator runs; the response lands at $HG_EVAL_RESPONSE. Omit when the evaluator owns the invocation itself (webhook, relay, cron). Mutually exclusive with invoke.

evaluate.description: Path (relative to the scenario directory, contained within it) to the deterministic evaluator executable. Repository-owned code: untrusted (cloned) sources require --allow-repo-scripts. Optional when expect: carries the whole assertion; required otherwise.

timeout.description: Hard wall-clock budget in seconds for one run, prompt included. Defaults to the suite's, then 300.

repeat.description: Runs per invocation, each recorded independently — for surfacing nondeterminism by hand, not for retry-until-green.

required.description: Defaults to true. false makes the scenario informational: it runs and reports but never fails the suite.

setup.description: Shell commands run in order from the scenario directory before each run. Repository-owned code, trust-gated like `evaluate`.

cleanup.description: Shell commands run from the scenario directory after each run — ALWAYS, including on timeout and evaluator crash.

invoke.description: Typed communication invocation, executed by the runner BEFORE the evaluator through the same engine as hg event emit / ingress test. Exactly one form.

event.description: Publish one event from a payload file through the communication engine.

name.description: Event type, version suffix optional (observability.alert matches observability.alert/v1).

from.description: Producer as <profile>/<app>#<output>; required only when the event has several producers.

payload.description: Payload JSON file, relative to the scenario directory and contained within it.

toAgent.description: Narrow the fan-out to one agent profile.

toChatops.description: Narrow the fan-out to one ChatOps space.

events.description: A FIFO sequence: payloads emitted in order through the same producer.

name.description: Event type, version suffix optional (observability.alert matches observability.alert/v1).

from.description: Producer as <profile>/<app>#<output>; required only when the event has several producers.

orderingKey.description: Override the producer's subject with this value in every payload - the whole sequence shares one ordering group.

payloads.description: Ordered payload files; one event is emitted per file, first to last.

items.description: Payload JSON file, relative to the scenario directory and contained within it.

externalWebhook.description: Deliver a signed request to a declared external webhook binding, exercising the gateway's verification path - including its negative modes.

binding.description: An externalInputs[] name declared by the repository.

payload.description: Payload JSON file, relative to the scenario directory and contained within it.

duplicate.description: Send the identical signed request twice; the second must be rejected as a replay.

expect.description: Runner-checked expectations against the invocation's terminal receipts - infrastructure truths (which destinations accepted). Business behavior stays in the evaluator.

outputs.description: Destinations that must show an accepted terminal receipt; any listed destination without one fails the scenario.

agent.description: An agent destination: the named profile must show an accepted delivery receipt.

rejected.description: For negative externalWebhook modes: the request must be rejected with exactly this reason, and nothing may be delivered.
